analysis: The only changes in MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift are two call sites (head lines 963-964 and 1074) that add `onRefusal: budget.directChargeRefusalSignal()` to MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation construction. One is in prepareDecodedMedia's authorize closure, the other in beginEncodedMediaReservation. The rest of the file is unchanged context. Registry/transaction lock ordering, lifecycle checks, fault retention and reservation retention in `mediaReservations` (lines 967 and 1075) are untouched. The argument is evaluated before the reservation is created and retained, so it adds no new ownership gap. The new callback is a refusal notification from the ledger charge path. The supplied evidence does not show what directChargeRefusalSignal() does, whether it runs under the ledger lock or a transaction lock, or whether it can reenter the registry. Because the file's documented lock order is registry -> transaction -> permit/ledger, I checked these call sites. Line 967 and the reservation constructors run the charge outside `lock`, since `lock.withLock` only wraps the dictionary insert. At line 1071 the construction also runs outside any lock, so no lock-order inversion is visible from this file. Unverified contract: the GlobalKVCacheBudget.directChargeRefusalSignal and MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation init implementations (not supplied) must not do native work, block, or leak refusal detail beyond the host. No threat-model regression (T-041 cache surface, A-001 prompt data, TB-007) is established from this diff. The signal presumably serves availability or reclaim, i.e. an internal refusal path.
